clue.text: New dawn breaks very pale in due course

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'as and when' means at whatever time something happens, which is in due course.

parts.note: a run is some exercise
to sit for an artist is to model; SIT backwards
h = hot, on taps

explanation.surface: A tiny fashion model came back hot after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a noun, a person; it is a verb, to sit for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the runt of a litter: small and undersized.

clue.text: Wavering voter found valuables

indicators.note: moving unsteadily, so the letters shift

parts.note: VOTER rearranged

explanation.surface: A floating voter comes across some valuables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the verb of a treasure find; it joins wordplay to definition, and nods to treasure trove.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from treasure trove: a found hoard of precious things.

clue.text: Naturalist who named Arcida, new order for ark clam

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the seven letters of ARK CLAM rearranged

explanation.surface: A naturalist gave the ark clams a new order, Arcida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a taxonomic order, and Arcida really is the order of ark clams, which Lamarck named.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck, French naturalist, named many invertebrate groups including Arcida.

clue.text: Expedition eats most of sandwiches, cake etc

indicators.note: most of a thing is all but a little of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: has = eats, as in 'has lunch'
sandwiches and cake make afternoon TEA; drop the last letter

explanation.surface: An expedition party polishes off most of the picnic sandwiches and cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' reads as a journey; it also means speed, as in expeditious. Afternoon tea is a British light meal of sandwiches and cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition in its older sense is promptness, haste.

clue.text: Weed earl cleared out on estate

indicators.note: the inside is emptied, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: an estate's grounds
EarL with its middle removed

explanation.surface: An earl, turfed out, is weeding his estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleared out' reads as an earl evicted from his estate; it empties EARL of its inside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small yellow-flowered plant that gardeners pull up on sight.
